title: What does Federal Reserve SR 08-8 expect of compliance training at large banking organizations?
description: Federal Reserve SR 08-8 compliance risk management: training throughout the organization, the $50 billion marker and guidance status, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Federal Reserve supervisory letter SR 08-8 / CA 08-11 (October 16, 2008) expects banking organizations with $50 billion or more in consolidated assets and complex compliance profiles to run firmwide compliance risk management programs that include compliance training throughout the organization. Senior management should communicate the importance of compliance at all levels through ongoing training. SR 08-8 is supervisory guidance: it does not have the force and effect of law.
keyTakeaways: SR 08-8 says a firmwide compliance program should establish the framework for identifying, assessing, controlling, measuring, monitoring and reporting compliance risks, and for providing compliance training throughout the organization.

Banking organizations with $50 billion or more in consolidated total assets, and foreign banking organizations with $50 billion or more in US third-party assets, should generally implement firmwide programs with a corporate compliance function.
Senior management "should communicate the importance of compliance across, and at all levels of, the organization through ongoing training and other means."
The letter was revised on February 26, 2021 to align board expectations with SR 21-3, and on October 1, 2025 to remove references to reputational risk.
Under 12 CFR Part 262 Appendix A, supervisory guidance does not have the force and effect of law and the Board does not take enforcement actions based on supervisory guidance.
regulator: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Federal Reserve)
appliesTo: Banking organizations supervised by the Federal Reserve, with specific expectations for those with $50 billion or more in consolidated total assets and complex compliance profiles
Foreign banking organizations for their US operations, with $50 billion or more in US third-party assets generally treated as large and complex
Boards of directors and senior management, including the corporate compliance function
Compliance staff in corporate, business line and local roles

sections.heading: What is SR 08-8 and is it binding?

blocks.text: [SR 08-8 / CA 08-11, Compliance Risk Management Programs and Oversight at Large Banking Organizations with Complex Compliance Profiles](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR0808.htm), is a Federal Reserve supervisory letter dated October 16, 2008. It clarifies the Federal Reserve's views on firmwide compliance risk management, compliance independence, monitoring and testing, and the respective roles of the board and senior management. The letter says the Federal Reserve's expectations are in line with the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's April 2005 paper, Compliance and the compliance function in banks.

SR 08-8 is guidance, not a regulation. The Board's statement on the role of supervisory guidance, at [12 CFR Part 262, Appendix A](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/12/appendix-A_to_part_262), says that unlike a law or regulation, supervisory guidance "does not have the force and effect of law, and the Board does not take enforcement actions based on supervisory guidance." In practice, examiners use SR 08-8 to assess whether compliance risk management is sound, and weaknesses can lead to supervisory findings that refer to underlying laws and regulations.

The letter has been revised twice. On February 26, 2021 it was revised, as described in SR 21-4 / CA 21-2, to better reflect the Board's guidance on board effectiveness in SR 21-3 and SR 16-11. On October 1, 2025 it was revised to remove references to reputational risk. This page reflects the letter as published on federalreserve.gov as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Which organizations does SR 08-8 apply to?

blocks.text: All Federal Reserve-supervised organizations should have effective compliance risk management programs tailored to their risk profiles, but the specific firmwide expectations target large organizations with complex compliance profiles. The letter states that, although balance sheet size is not the defining indication, organizations with $50 billion or more in consolidated total assets typically have multiple legal entities that call for a comprehensive firmwide approach, and should generally implement firmwide compliance risk management programs and have a corporate compliance function.

Large organizations with less complex profiles, for example few legal entities and a very limited range of activities, may manage compliance risk without a comprehensive firmwide approach, or with one focused on particular firmwide risks, relying on executive and management committees for oversight. Foreign banking organizations with $50 billion or more in US third-party assets are generally treated as large and complex for their US operations unless those activities are less complex.

The letter names anti-money laundering, privacy, affiliate transactions, conflicts of interest and fair lending as areas where requirements cross business lines and legal entities. Training on those topics is covered on the [BSA/AML training](/regulations/bsa-aml-training-requirements) and [fair lending and UDAAP training](/regulations/fair-lending-and-udaap-training) pages.

sections.heading: What does SR 08-8 say about compliance training?

blocks.text: Training appears in three places, and together they make it a core program element rather than an add-on. First, the processes for managing compliance risk firmwide "should be formalized in a compliance program that establishes the framework for identifying, assessing, controlling, measuring, monitoring, and reporting compliance risks across the organization, and for providing compliance training throughout the organization."

Second, compliance programs at large organizations with complex profiles should include more extensive processes for those same functions, including "providing compliance training throughout the organization in order to appropriately control the heightened level and complexity of compliance risk." The same expectation is stated for foreign banking organizations with large, complex US operations, scaled to their US risk profile.

blocks.title: SR 08-8, Section IV, Senior Management
blocks.text: "Senior management should communicate the importance of compliance across, and at all levels of, the organization through ongoing training and other means."

Third, as the callout shows, senior management owns the message. The letter also states that the primary responsibility for complying with applicable rules and standards rests with the individuals within the organization as they conduct their day-to-day activities. That principle is the strongest argument for role-based training: people cannot carry primary responsibility for rules they have not been taught in the context of their own work. See [role-based training](/glossary/role-based-training).

sections.heading: What are the board's and senior management's roles?

blocks.text: The board oversees and senior management implements. Under SR 08-8 the board should oversee the development of, review, approve and periodically monitor the firm's compliance strategy; tell senior management what information it needs about compliance risks and program effectiveness; hold senior management accountable for implementation and timely resolution of issues; and promote the stature and independence of the corporate compliance function with appropriate resources.

Senior management should be fully capable, qualified and properly motivated to manage compliance risks; implement and enforce compliance policies and standards; integrate compliance objectives into management goals and compensation; and apply disciplinary measures for serious compliance failures. The corporate compliance function should report to the board or a committee on significant compliance matters and program effectiveness. Training metrics are a natural component of that reporting; see [how to report training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board).

sections.heading: How do independence and testing expectations affect compliance staff development?

blocks.text: SR 08-8 expects compliance staff to be appropriately independent of the business lines they cover, and that shapes how compliance staff are managed and developed. In dual reporting structures, the corporate compliance function should play a key role in personnel decisions and actions, including remuneration, affecting business line and local compliance staff. The letter states plainly that compliance staff "should not be compensated on the basis of the financial performance of the business line."

On testing, SR 08-8 says risk assessments are the foundation of an effective compliance monitoring and testing program, and that the scope and frequency of testing should follow the assessed risk of each business activity. Periodic testing by compliance staff is strongly encouraged. Compliance staff who test controls need training in testing methods as well as in the rules, and training gaps found in testing should feed back into the training plan. See [how to evidence training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator).

sections.heading: How can a banking organization map SR 08-8 expectations to evidence?

blocks.text: Because SR 08-8 states expectations rather than rules, the evidence question is how an organization would show examiners that it meets them. The table below is an original planning aid mapping each training-related expectation to the accountable party, the timing implied, and supporting evidence.

blocks.text: National banks under the OCC have a regulatory counterpart in the heightened standards; see [OCC heightened standards talent and training](/regulations/occ-heightened-standards-talent-and-training). A general method for building the firmwide map is in [how to map training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry builds the compliance obligations register, the legal entity and business line structure, and the role map first, then defines the knowledge each role needs before training is written. That makes "training throughout the organization" demonstrable: each module traces to an obligation, a role and a risk assessment. See the [financial services](/industries/financial-services) page.

faqs.q: Does SR 08-8 require a specific amount of compliance training?
faqs.a: No. SR 08-8 sets no hours, frequency or syllabus. It expects compliance training throughout the organization as part of a firmwide program, scaled to the complexity of compliance risk, and ongoing training as a means for senior management to communicate the importance of compliance.

faqs.q: Does SR 08-8 apply to banks under $50 billion?
faqs.a: The letter states that all supervised organizations should have effective compliance risk management programs tailored to their risk profiles. Its specific firmwide program and corporate compliance function expectations are aimed at organizations with $50 billion or more and complex compliance profiles.

faqs.q: Can the Federal Reserve enforce SR 08-8 directly?
faqs.a: No. Under 12 CFR Part 262 Appendix A, supervisory guidance does not have the force and effect of law and the Board does not take enforcement actions based on it. Examiners may still use the guidance to assess risk management and cite related violations of laws and regulations.

faqs.q: What changed in the October 2025 revision?
faqs.a: The Federal Reserve's page for SR 08-8 states that on October 1, 2025 the letter was revised to remove references to reputational risk. The training, independence, testing and board and senior management expectations remain.
